answer: An agent economy sells a small atlas of admission seats each epoch by sealed-bid, every bid burned on-chain. A farm spreading into many aliases must buy one seat per clone, and its own swelling demand becomes a mirror, reflecting a higher uniform clearing price onto every seat it already holds. Cost per alias therefore climbs with the farm's own size, while honest agents arriving as a thin zephyr of bids pay only the low floor. Settlement reprices the round and burns each winning bid, so no coalition can pool, resell, or recycle a seat.
